search.description: Search tickets, users, organizations and groups with Zendesk search syntax, for example 'type:ticket status:open'. A ticket comes back with its subject, description (what the customer wrote), status, priority, and the name and email of its assignee and requester, the day it was created and how many days it has waited (created_display and days_waiting, beta; hours_waiting and waiting_display such as '5 hours', beta), who has it (assignee_display, the name or Unassigned, beta), and ticket_link, the page that opens it in Zendesk (beta). For tickets still waiting for a first reply, turn on 'Only tickets with no agent reply yet' (beta). To react to each new ticket, start the workflow with the New ticket trigger instead of searching on a schedule.

results.description: The printer in accounting is smoking.
results.subject: Printer on fire

search.name: search

parameters.description: What to look for. Zendesk search syntax works here, such as type:ticket status:open priority:urgent. To look back from now, write the time with no spaces, such as created>30minutes or updated>2days; created<2days is older than two days. solved>7days finds tickets solved in the last week (updated> also catches tickets edited after they were solved). status<solved means new, open, pending or on hold, and assignee:none finds tickets nobody has taken. Beta: satisfaction:bad finds tickets a customer rated bad, satisfaction:badwithcomment those where they also wrote why, and satisfaction:good the ones rated good.

examples.label: Tickets created in the last 30 minutes
Unassigned tickets older than two days

parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Which field to order results by. Defaults to relevance.
parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.description: Which end of the list to start from.
parameters.name: sort_order

parameters.description: Which page of results to read. Zendesk returns at most 1,000 results, so pages run from 1 to 10.
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: How many records to return (1-100). Leave it out and you get the first 25, so set 100 when a list or digest should show everything that matches.
parameters.name: per_page

parameters.description: Beta. On keeps only the tickets no agent has publicly replied to, whatever their status: the question behind 'waiting for a first reply' and first-reply SLA checks, which status:new misses once a ticket is assigned or has an internal note. Combine it with a time in the search terms (type:ticket status<solved created<4hours for tickets unanswered after 4 hours). The results are then tickets only, and count is how many on this page.
parameters.display_name: Only tickets with no agent reply yet
parameters.name: only_unanswered

assignee_display.description: Beta. On a ticket: who has it, as a digest line says it: the assignee's name, or Unassigned.

created_display.description: Beta. On a ticket: the day it was created as a person writes it, such as Nov 6, 2026, for a message or digest.

days_waiting.description: Beta. On a ticket: whole days since it was created, for a digest of tickets that have waited too long.

hours_waiting.description: Beta. On a ticket: whole hours since it was created, for an hours-long reply target such as 4 hours.

ticket_link.description: Beta. On a ticket: the link that opens it in Zendesk, for a message or digest. The url field is the API address, not this.

waiting_display.description: Beta. On a ticket: how long it has waited as a person says it, such as 45 minutes, 5 hours or 3 days, for a message or digest.

status.description: Status of the action execution ("success" on success).

zendesk_new_organization_trigger.description: Runs for each new organization (a customer company) in Zendesk. Organizations already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.domain_names: The email domains that put people in it.
output.name: Its name.

zendesk_new_ticket_in_view_trigger.description: Runs when a ticket appears in one of your Zendesk views, such as Unassigned tickets or a team's queue: a new ticket, or one that changed to match it. One that leaves the view and comes back runs again. Tickets in it when the workflow is turned on don't start it. Watches views of up to 1,000 tickets. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.assignee_name: The agent it is assigned to, empty if nobody.
output.priority: How urgent it is: low, normal, high or urgent; empty if not set.
output.requester_first_name: Beta. The first word of requester_name, ready for 'Hi Ada,' in a reply with no step to split the name.
output.status: The ticket's status, such as new or open.
output.subject: The ticket's subject.

parameters.description: The view to watch. Pick one of the views you can see in Zendesk.
parameters.name: view_id

zendesk_new_ticket_trigger.description: Runs for each new Zendesk ticket, with what the customer wrote and who sent it. Tickets already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.assignee_name: The agent it is assigned to, empty if nobody.
output.priority: How urgent it is: low, normal, high or urgent; empty if not set.
output.requester_first_name: Beta. The first word of requester_name, ready for 'Hi Ada,' in a reply with no step to split the name.
output.status: The ticket's status, such as new or open.
output.subject: The ticket's subject.

parameters.description: Beta. Only tickets created with this priority: low, normal, high or urgent, or several separated by commas (high, urgent), so an urgent-ticket alert needs no check of its own. Leave empty to run for every new ticket.

zendesk_new_user_trigger.description: Runs for each new person in Zendesk: a customer who writes in or signs up, or a new agent. Use its role to tell them apart. People already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.email: Their email address, empty if none.

output.name: Their name.
output.organization_id: The organization they belong to, if any.
output.phone: Their phone number, empty if none.
output.role: end-user for a customer, agent or admin for staff.

zendesk_satisfaction_rating_trigger.description: Runs when a customer rates a Zendesk ticket good or bad in the satisfaction survey, with their comment, the ticket and who handled it. Set Score to bad to follow up on unhappy customers. Runs once per ticket and score: a customer who changes good to bad starts it again, one who only adds a comment doesn't. Ratings given before the workflow is turned on don't start it. Zendesk shows ratings only to admins, so whoever connected Zendesk must be a Zendesk admin. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.assignee_name: The agent the ticket is assigned to, empty if nobody.
output.comment: What the customer wrote with the rating, empty if nothing.
output.organization_name: The customer's organization (company), empty if none.
output.rated_at: When they rated it, such as 2026-11-20T14:05:00Z.
output.rated_display: The day they rated it, ready to read: Nov 20, 2026.
output.reason: The reason the customer picked for a bad rating, such as 'The issue was not resolved', empty if none.
output.requester_first_name: The first word of requester_name, ready for 'Hi Ada,'.
output.score: What the customer chose: bad or good.
output.ticket_url: The ticket's page in Zendesk, for agents, such as https://acme.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/123.

parameters.description: Only ratings with this score: bad or good. Leave it empty for both.
parameters.name: score

Runs once per ticket, so later replies to an urgent ticket don't start it again. Tickets already at that priority when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.
